tools.description: The 19 categories this API scores spending against. Call this first and map the person's statement onto these ids before calling simulate_cards.

tools.name: simulate_cards
tools.description: Given a year of spending by category, returns the three best credit cards and the best two-card combination, with what each is worth after its annual fee over the chosen horizon. tools.name: keep_or_cancel
tools.description: For cards the person already carries, says whether each one still earns its annual fee back on their spending, and what to move to if not. Pass the cards as `held`. Returns a verdict and a rounded yearly margin.

tools.name: compare_two
tools.description: Two named cards head to head on the person's own spending: which one pays more, and by how much a year. Use this when they are choosing between two specific cards. For 'what should I get', use simulate_cards instead.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "spending_categories" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: The 19 categories this API scores spending against. Call this first and map the person's statement onto these ids before calling simulate_cards.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
